## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Particles
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Particle force fields
//  - Particle systems
//  - Cloth, rope, and fluids

//==
// # Particle force fields
//
// The accelerations applied to particles each step: gravity, drag, vortices,
// attractors, curl-noise turbulence, and wind. These types are expressed in
// 3D; planar systems interpret them in the XY plane and ignore Z components.
// Accelerations are in meters per second squared.

// Constant acceleration applied to every particle, in meters per second
// squared (e.g. (0, -9.81, 0)).
type ParticleGravity
    implements IValue
{
    Acceleration: Vector3D;
}

// Velocity-opposing deceleration of particles: acceleration =
// -(LinearCoefficient * v + QuadraticCoefficient * |v| * v).
// LinearCoefficient is in units of one per second; QuadraticCoefficient is in
// units of one per meter.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_(physics))
type ParticleDrag
    implements IValue
{
    LinearCoefficient: Number;
    QuadraticCoefficient: Number;
}

// A swirling force field: particles are accelerated tangentially around the
// line through Center along Axis. Strength is the tangential acceleration in
// meters per second squared at one meter from the axis, diminishing with
// distance.
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vortex)
type ParticleVortex
    implements IValue
{
    Center: Point3D;
    Axis: Direction3D;
    Strength: Number;
}

// A point force field: particles inside FalloffRadius accelerate toward
// Center. Strength is the peak acceleration in meters per second squared at
// the center, fading to zero at FalloffRadius; negative values repel.
type ParticleAttractor
    implements IValue
{
    Center: Point3D;
    Strength: Number;
    FalloffRadius: Length;
}

// Curl-noise turbulence applied to particles. SpatialFrequency is the noise
// frequency in cycles per meter; Strength is the peak acceleration in meters
// per second squared; Seed selects the noise realization.
type ParticleTurbulence
    implements IValue
{
    SpatialFrequency: Number;
    Strength: Number;
    Seed: Integer;
}

// A steady wind with gusts. Speed is the mean wind speed along Direction;
// Turbulence is the dimensionless gust strength as a proportion of Speed in
// [0, 1]; GustFrequency is how often gust cycles occur.
type WindModel
    implements IValue
{
    Direction: Direction3D;
    Speed: Speed;
    Turbulence: Number;
    GustFrequency: Frequency;
}

// The whole force set acting on a simulation, with no particles attached.
// `ParticleSystem3D` below carries these same six arrays inline; this type is
// the bundle on its own, so anything that is stepped but is not a particle
// system — a cloth, a rope, a soft body — takes the identical force vocabulary
// instead of declaring a second one. `Forces` (`particles.library.plato`)
// projects a system onto it, and `AccelerationAt` there sums it.
//
// Winds are not summed with the rest: a wind is a VELOCITY field, and it enters
// through the drag term as a relative velocity. See the force-set section of
// `particles.library.plato`.
type ParticleForces3D
    implements IValue
{
    Gravities: Array<ParticleGravity>;
    Drags: Array<ParticleDrag>;
    Vortices: Array<ParticleVortex>;
    Attractors: Array<ParticleAttractor>;
    Turbulences: Array<ParticleTurbulence>;
    Winds: Array<WindModel>;
}

//==
// # Particle systems
//
// Particles, the emitters that spawn them, and the complete planar and
// spatial systems owning both together with their force fields. Positions are
// in meters, velocities in meters per second, masses in kilograms.

//==
// # Particles

// One planar particle. Velocity is in meters per second; Size is the world
// diameter in meters; Rotation is the sprite spin angle and AngularVelocity
// its rate; a particle dies when Age reaches Lifetime.
type Particle2D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point2D;
    Velocity: Vector2D;
    Age: Duration;
    Lifetime: Duration;
    Size: Number;
    Color: Color;
    Rotation: Angle;
    AngularVelocity: AngularVelocity;
    Mass: Mass;
}

// One spatial particle. Velocity is in meters per second; Size is the world
// diameter in meters; Rotation is the billboard spin angle about the view
// axis and AngularVelocity its rate; a particle dies when Age reaches
// Lifetime.
type Particle3D
    implements IValue
{
    Position: Point3D;
    Velocity: Vector3D;
    Age: Duration;
    Lifetime: Duration;
    Size: Number;
    Color: Color;
    Rotation: Angle;
    AngularVelocity: AngularVelocity;
    Mass: Mass;
}
```
